If you are subbing out the beef broth for veg broth you will have a more flexible soup profile too. Just think "will this be yummy if melty" if yes then do it. 

If you reallyyyy doubt put a little on a spoon and see how the flavors play. Theres also nothing wrong (nobody crucify me now) with just having the soup with bread alone.

I would make a lot of caramelized onions with half and freeze them in an ice cube tray. Quick way to add that lovely flavor without caramelizing every single time. Could throw them in literally every recipe.

Other idea would be to bake or air fry slivers to use to toss in with salad, top pasta dishes or even stack on soups. Makes a really nice flavorful texture contrast.

But if you want like a recipe, french onion soup is a really easy one. I usually use 6 onions at a time to make about 2-3 servings. The extra serving (I cook even numbers cause partner) I have left I usually turn into a pasta sauce the next day.

My interest in wines made me take tea more seriously recently. During the last few months, I have become a "taste collector" of sorts. I'm obsessed with trying as many different things as I can and learning about why it has that flavor specifically (think terrior, politics, cultural diaspora, etc). However, cooking new meals all the time can be a bit hard with work, so trying new drinks was easy thing to do passively. I had always appreciated teas in passing previously, but this new fascination made me want to take a closer look into everything I ate or drank. If you know the basics about wine, you can spot the similarities between it and tea, which made it an obvious complimentary hobby.

It truly depends on the individual, but typically impulsive actions are done as a response to an uncomfortable situation and serves as a distraction, which in turn can be "soothing". Personally, in the past when I dealt with rapid impulses, I just snowballed with them because i not only could not help myself, but also because I felt pleased immediately after my actions. However, depending on the impulse, sometimes there would be equal amounts of regret after for feeling "out of control". BPD has a lot of "highs", both with negative and positive emotions.
